enkephalin-like peptides are selectively expressed in dermal CD-68 positive macrophages in human skin, and that there is an increase of enkephalin positive cells in lesional skin in psoriasis.
enkephaline-like immunoreactivity is selectively expressed in CD68-positive cells in human skin.
Enkephalins are present in monocytes and macrophages in psoriastic lesions and that this may play an important role in the regulation in the inflammatory processes seen.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the localization of opioid peptides in human skin, the identification of the cell type producing these peptides and the quantification of their levels in psoriasis, which is a chronic inflammatory skin disease.
the presence and distribution of opioid peptides, especially enkephaline, in normal human skin, and in skin from patients with psoriasis.
the expression of opioid peptides in the skin and their possible role in inflammatory skin diseases.

the enkephalinergic system in human skin is localized to a subpopulation of CD68-positive dermal macrophages/ monocytes, and that these cells are activated in psoriasis.
enkephaline-like activity is increased in psoriasis.

enkephalines in human skin are produced by macrophages and are increased in lesional psoriatic skin.
enkephalin-like material is present in a subset of macrophages/ monocytes in human skin.
enkephalin-like material is produced and stored in a subset of CD68-positive cells in human dermis.
